newsitem.title: USA: UAL's United March load factor rises.
newsitem.headline: UAL's United March load factor rises.

text.p: UAL Corp's United Airlines said Tuesday its passenger load factor for March rose to 74.0 percent from 72.9 percent a year ago.
The load factor for its North American routes rose 1.8 points to 73.3 percent, and its Latin American load factor increased by 1.9 points to 64.8 percent.
The passenger load factor for the Pacific routes fell 0.2 points to 74.8 percent, while Atlantic load factor dropped 1.2 points to 82.3 percent, United said.
Year-to-date, United's pasenger load factor was 69.9 percent, up from 68.7 percent a year ago.

For March, revenue passenger miles for its scheduled service rose 5.1 percent to 10.39 billion from 9.89 billion. This included a 5.6 percent rise in North American revenue passenger miles to 6.53 billion, and a 10.6 percent increase in Atlantic revenue passenger miles to 1.03 billion.

March available seat miles for its scheduled service increased by 3.5 percent to 14.04 billion, including a 3.1 percent rise in North America to 8.91 billion. Atlantic available seat miles rose 12.1 percent to 1.25 billion.
Cargo ton miles for March gained 11.8 percent to 227.7 million.

"We are pleased with the overall traffic performance for March," John Edwardson, president, said in a statement. "Moreover, with the strong fare environment and United's focus on the high-yield passenger, we continue to anticipate a healthy year-over-year increase in unit revenue (total revenues divided by available seat miles) for March."
